title: Shrinkage priors on interactions do not give honest intervals for a transported effect
question: Do posterior intervals from shrinkage or selection priors on treatment-by-covariate interactions keep frequentist coverage for the transported effect when the whole procedure is repeated?
design: Continuous-outcome STC with eight candidate interactions, one strong or three moderate modifiers, two sample sizes; flat, empirical-Bayes ridge, hierarchical normal, spike-and-slab averaging and median-probability-model priors. 4 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: No. Continuous shrinkage does not select, but its intervals still undercovered: 95% posterior intervals for the transported effect covered 0.794 to 0.948 with an empirical-Bayes ridge prior and 0.868 to 0.959 with a hierarchical normal prior, against 0.939 to 0.955 for a flat prior. When the interactions the target weights push the effect the same way, their joint shrinkage biases the transported effect (up to 0.19) and the narrower interval does not carry the bias. Integrating the prior scale recovers only part of the loss.
findings: Worst cell, three moderate modifiers at 100 per arm: empirical-Bayes ridge 0.794, hierarchical normal 0.868, spike-and-slab averaging 0.908, median-probability model 0.785, flat 0.954.
Plugging in the fitted prior scale costs up to 0.074 coverage relative to integrating it; the remainder is prior-truth conflict at a fixed nonzero truth.
The median-probability model's conditional interval, the Bayesian form of DEC-11's selection, was the worst prior at 300 per arm (0.840 with three moderate modifiers).
With one strong modifier at 300 per arm every prior except the median-probability model covered at least 0.948.
not_answered: Continuous outcome with conjugate priors; no horseshoe, heredity constraints or projection-predictive selection; aligned modifiers only, no null scenario. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target-population mean difference, A versus C, -0.5 + 0.5 times the sum of the interactions
